details.description: Gemma 2B-it is the instruction-tuned, 2-billion-parameter model in Google's first-generation Gemma family of lightweight open-weight models, built from the same research as Google's Gemini models, per Google's model card. It is a decoder-only, text-to-text model tuned for chat-style tasks such as question answering, summarization, and reasoning, over an 8,192-token context window, with English-language training data drawn from web documents, code, and mathematical text. Google's current Gemma documentation lists Gemma 4 as the newest generation and groups this first-generation model among "previous Gemma models," though its weights remain downloadable.
advantages: Instruction-tuned for chat-style tasks including question answering, summarization, and reasoning, per Google's model card.
Lightweight at 2B parameters, positioned for deployment on resource-constrained hardware such as laptops, per Google's model card.
Open weights available for download and local fine-tuning, per Google's model card.
disadvantages: Superseded by three newer Gemma generations; Google's documentation now lists Gemma 4 as the current generation and groups this model under "previous Gemma models."
Trained and documented for English-language use only, per Google's model card.
Google publishes general reasoning benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval) for this model family only on the base pretrained checkpoint, not the instruction-tuned model.
use_cases: General text generation and creative writing

notes: Google's Gemma 1 model card gives the MMLU/HellaSwag/HumanEval/GSM8K benchmark table only for the pretrained (PT) checkpoints, not the instruction-tuned (IT) ones; the IT-specific tables on that page cover only toxicity/bias metrics (RealToxicity, BBQ, CrowS-Pairs, Winogender, etc.), which the evaluations rules exclude (not accuracy-style or the wrong direction), so evaluations is left empty for this exact (IT) model rather than borrowing the base checkpoint's scores.
